control_room.route: GET /api/v1/matters/{matterId}/control-room (existing candidate route; response shape now specified)

READ-01.decision: Server-assembled display projection evaluated in ONE read snapshot (ADR-002 §1.6 REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY). No persisted ControlRoom entity, store, cache, realtime channel or background pipeline
READ-01.rationale: FR-009 Validation 'summary ties to same scope/as-of' and AC-109 'match underlying authorized records at that boundary' require one boundary; client composition of N reads yields mixed snapshots and N authorization checks. Detail is fetched lazily through typed reads

READ-02.decision: One meta.asOf/sourceRevision for every AVAILABLE section. Per-section availability AVAILABLE|UNAVAILABLE only. STALE is not a server value: it is the client's label on a previously received response retained after a failed refetch, shown with that response's asOf. Root HTTP 200 when at least one section is AVAILABLE; 503 /problems/unavailable when the snapshot cannot be opened or no section is available. Each section bounded with server order, nextCursor for continuation on its named collection route; continuation pages are new snapshots with their own asOf/sourceRevision and are never silently merged as coherent
READ-02.rationale: Satisfies FR-009 error behaviour (partial region explicit, never zero blockers from failure) without a retained-data store, which no architecture document selects

READ-03.decision: Small typed cards + typed refs {kind, id}; detail via reviewed catalogue; reuse candidate identity/provenance/axes/problem conventions; INT-A refId/value/16KiB envelope not used
READ-03.rationale: Avoids duplicating domain objects and keeps Requirement/Action, criterion/Evidence and exact version/cycle identity

control_room.meta: {matterRef:{kind:MATTER,id}, asOf (server RFC3339 with offset), sourceRevision (integer matter event seq), historyMaterializedThrough (integer seq)}; correlation via X-Request-ID response header
control_room.section_envelope: {availability: AVAILABLE|UNAVAILABLE, items: [card] | null, total: int|null, nextCursor: string|null, unavailableReason: code|null}
invariants: AVAILABLE+[] = successful authorized zero; UNAVAILABLE+null = failed evaluation, never zero/READY
A 200 response does not mean every section is available; consumers inspect each section
condition exception counts sourced from an UNAVAILABLE section are null, never 0 (FR-009 'do not display zero blockers from failure')
A section nextCursor is a cursor for that section's named continuation route; the route's default order for that filter equals the section order, so continuation reaches every row
condition.completeness=INCOMPLETE if any contributing section is UNAVAILABLE
Counts/totals are in-Matter from the same snapshot; valid because P0 has no sub-Matter ACL (permission-matrix); a future narrower access rule reopens this
Section page sizes are an implementation parameter <= inherited candidate cap 200; no new numeric limit is set here
Reads create no domain event, verification or history; denial goes to restricted security audit only

condition.rule: Named exceptions only, codes from approved vocabularies (CRITICAL_ATTENTION, DEPENDENCY_BLOCKED, OVERDUE, DUE_SOON, COMPLETED_UNVERIFIED, DISPUTED, EVIDENCE_GAP, WAITING, OPEN_DECISION, MILESTONE_UNASSESSED, MILESTONE_NOT_READY); counts from the same snapshot. No overall status enum, score or percentage. completeness=INCOMPLETE whenever any contributing section is UNAVAILABLE, and every exception sourced from an UNAVAILABLE section has count:null (never 0)

blockers.order: critical-unsatisfied first (dependency-engine §5), then rootCause before intermediate, then dueAt ascending (no due last), then id
blockers.card: {ref: REQUIREMENT|ACTION, label, axes, ownerRef, dueAt, waitRef|null, rootCause: bool, failingGates:[{edgeRef, downstreamRef, gate, failed:[code]}], criticalMilestoneRefs, revision}
blockers.rule: Cards are unsatisfied upstream CAUSES: every node with at least one failing outgoing gate. rootCause=true when the cause itself is dependency READY (e.g. AtlasT0 RQ-04 WAITING+READY failing DEP-01). The card shows the cause's own axes and wait, so WAITING and BLOCKED stay distinct. Blocked targets and transitive impact via DR-06
blockers.continuation: GET /api/v1/matters/{matterId}/blockers (new candidate; same card and order)

nextActions.order: RULE-021: critical-unsatisfied, dueAt asc (no due last), id
nextActions.card: {ref: ACTION, label, ownerRef, dueAt, axes, permittedActions?}; section adds excluded:[{ref, reason: WAITING|BLOCKED|UNASSIGNED}]
nextActions.rule: Backend RULE-021 candidates only; excluded reasons always returned so an empty list explains itself (AtlasT0). Requirements never appear

waitingOn.order: followUpDueAt ascending (none last), then openedAt, then id
waitingOn.card: {ref: WAIT, subjectRef, partyRef|condition, internalOwnerRef, reason, followUpDueAt, openedAt, openedEventSeq}
waitingOn.rule: Subject dependency state is shown from the subject's own axes; WAITING never implies BLOCKED. openedAt/openedEventSeq identify the event that opened the wait (execution transition or filing observation, e.g. AUTHORITY_REVIEW); system-recorded time, not an asserted real-world start (TQ-06)

milestones.card: {ref: MILESTONE, label, dueAt, critical, readiness:{state: READY|NOT_READY|UNASSESSED, satisfied, total, unsatisfied:[{requirementRef, failed:[code]}]}}
milestones.rule: UNASSESSED (no declared prerequisites) is a successful AVAILABLE result, not UNAVAILABLE. No percentage

evidenceGaps.order: subject critical first, then subject dueAt, then id
evidenceGaps.card: {ref: EVIDENCE_REQUIREMENT, criterionRevisionRef, componentKey?, subjectRef, gap: MISSING|PENDING_REVIEW|REJECTED|EXPIRED|DISPUTED|WITHDRAWN, evidenceRefs (actual only)}
evidenceGaps.rule: A gap never carries a fabricated Evidence reference; criterion and Evidence stay distinct types

decisions.order: dueAt if recorded, then createdAt, then id
decisions.rule: Open decisions only; null owner shown as unassigned, never inferred. No override of dependency or proof

recentChanges.card: {eventRef, type, actorRef, recordedAt, effectiveAt, targetRef, correlationId}
recentChanges.rule: Most recent authorized events by seq; a still-open old blocker is not a change. Time-window mapping ('since T-1 09:00') remains TQ-05

embedded_groups.CRI-09: actionability: embedded. nextActions.excluded reasons + optional advisory permittedActions per card (absent = unknown, never allowed) + caller's own Matter role on DR-01. Backend enforces; TQ-03 per-claim verifier eligibility stays open
embedded_groups.CRI-10: navigation: embedded. Every card carries typed ref/relatedRefs resolved through the reviewed route table; no hrefs, no harness refId

reference.shape: {kind, id} (+ cycleNo for FILING_CYCLE where id = filingId; EVENT id = seq); matterId only in responses that span Matters (e.g. /me/actions)
rules: All refs in a Matter-scoped response belong to that Matter (RULE-003 no cross-matter links)
Exact identity retained: documentVersionId never replaced by current pointer; criterionRevisionId; claimId; (filingId, cycleNo) reusing candidate expectedCycleNo; submissionId
USER refs expose display name only for co-members of the Matter

read_common_rules: RC-1 Check order: authentication (401) -> Matter membership resolved from path or resource (404 uniform) -> query/cursor validation (422) -> evaluation (503). A revoked caller with a valid cursor gets 404
RC-2 No 403 on P0 reads; 403 remains for member role failures on commands only
RC-3 Resource-in-path routes resolve the owning Matter server-side; foreign or other-kind ids return the same 404
RC-4 Every response carries asOf/sourceRevision; singletons carry revision (+ETag) for later commands; GETs never take If-Match/If-None-Match (CI-02)
RC-5 Cache-Control: private, no-store; no shared cache of per-user legal data; no presigned content URLs
RC-6 Cursors are opaque, contain only keyset values of rows the caller could see, and are bound to actor/matter/collection/filter/sort; mismatch -> 422 without detail
RC-7 limit <= 200 inherited from candidate §1 (not a new approval); defaults are implementation parameters; in-Matter totals from the same snapshot allowed
RC-8 Derived axes and readiness are server values at asOf; clients never recompute them
RC-9 Reads create no domain event, verification or history; denials go to restricted security audit; X-Request-ID correlation; no tokens or legal payload in logs
RC-10 No product truncation contract; INT-A refId/value/16KiB rules are harness-only and not applied
